 ORDER

This is the second application filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 relating to FIR No 1593/2021 registered at P.S- Lasudia, Indore District- Indore (M.P.) for the offence under sections 363, 366, 376, 376 (2)(n), 376(3) of IPC and sections 3, 4, 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.

2/ As per prosecution story, on 04.12.2021 Complainant Achhelal Yadavfiled a report at police station Lasudia and mentioned that, he is the Father of the prosecutrix and the prosecutrix was Kuber Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3616165/

sentences.text: living with his family, today in the morning, the prosecutrix had gone to the Handpump to take bath but she did not return for a very long time and hence the family went out to look for her and Since they are unable to locate her.
After this the missing report was lodged at police station Lasudiaa district - Indore.
During the investigation the Prosecutrix was recovered on 09.01-2022, i,e, after more than a month of incidence which is 04/12/2021.
After her recovery, her statements were recorded and thereafter the present applicant/accused was implicated in the present case and the FIR was registered against him
3/ Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
Applicant is in custody since 09/01/2022.Applicant's
earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with a liberty to renew the prayer after examination of the prosecutrix before the trial Court.
The prosecutrix has been examined and as per her statement, it is clear that she went with the applicant with her own accord and consent.
The applicant and the prosecutrix were having love with each other and they agreed to get married after attaining the age of 18 years of the prosecutrix.
Applicant is 21 years young boy and is suffering jail incarceration since last two years.
He is permanent resident of District - Indore.
Final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
4/ Per-contra, learned PL for respondent - State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection.
5/ Learned counsel for the objector opposes the application and prays for its rejection by stating that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of the incident, therefore, her consent is immaterial.

6/ Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW-1) has been examined before the trial Court and she categorically deposed against the applicant in respect of the aforesaid offence; her statement is corroborated with her parents' statement (PW-2) and (PW-3); although the prosecutrix remained in company with the applicant for the period of 15-20 days and she travelled different places with him, but the prosecutrix is minor; her date of birth is 04/03/2008, therefore,
her consent is immaterial; in view of the material available on record against the applicant, at this stage, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
7/ Accordingly, this second bail application filed under section 439 of Cr.P.C has no force and is hereby dismissed.
